text:
alice (Support): FYI we started getting a bunch of 429s from customer-prod after last night's rate-cap change. they reported increased latency too. case #2438.

alice (Support): first noticed ~08:10 UTC, spike lasts ~3m and comes in bursts. customers see retries and some billing alerts.

tim (Support): can you share example request ids? we'll attach to the ticket and triage with platform.

alice (Support): sample req IDs: req_9a1c, req_9a2f, req_9a8b. payloads are typical chat generate calls, ~1k tokens.

jun (Eng Platform): got it. quick question — was the recent rate-policy rollout the staged one that reduced per-second token burst allowance from 10k->6k?

alice (Support): yes, that was the change pushed at 02:30 UTC. rollout was canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% last night.

lucas (Eng SRE): pulling metrics now. can you paste the 429 response body if any? sometimes we surface quota-type codes in headers.

alice (Support): header sample: "x-rate-limit-reason: token_burst_exceeded" and body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":12}

tim (Support): customers reporting retries escalate latency because client backoff is naive (fixed 1s). stacked retries cause downstream throttles.

jun (Eng Platform): looking at the rollout dashboard — we see error rate bump correlated with canary->50% step around 02:35 UTC for a subset of customers with bursty traffic. staging rules didn't include a per-customer burst exemption.

lucas (Eng SRE): related metric: downstream p95 token latency climbs when many clients hit retry loops. I'll run a short smoothing policy to limit global burst processing for 10m to avoid spike.

deploy-bot: rollout status changed: rate-policy-v2 -> 50% -> paused by jun at 02:41 UTC (automated health check failed). :rotating_light:

jun (Eng Platform): I paused the rollout when the canary health check crossed the error threshold. next steps: either rollback to previous policy or adjust policy to add per-customer burst window.

alice (Support): customer asks for ETA on fix. they have live traffic in EU region.

tim (Support): can we do a targeted rollback for that account/region quickly? they are on dedicated capacity but still hit the policy since the edge filter applies globally.

jun (Eng Platform): we have two options: 1) rollback policy globally to previous config (fast, 5m), 2) add an allowlist exception for that customer and re-run canary (10-20m). what is their SLA?

alice (Support): contract says high-availability, but not an explicit exception. they want low-latency restoration.

lucas (Eng SRE): my vote is targeted exception for their customer tag + rate smoothing for everyone for 15m. rollback risks reintroducing old cost behavior. we can also push a quick client-backoff guidance to customer meanwhile.

jun (Eng Platform): agreed. I'll create a temporary override: add tag filter rule to bypass token_burst_exceeded for acct:acme-inc for 30m. applying now.

deploy-bot: policy-override created by jun for acct:acme-inc (expires in 30m).

tim (Support): I messaged the customer to expect improvements within 2 minutes. also suggested exponential backoff and jitter in their SDK.

alice (Support): metrics show 429s for that acct dropping within ~90s. latency back to baseline in ~4m. customer confirmed faster responses. :thumbsup:

jun (Eng Platform): leaving the rollout paused. we'll re-run a smaller canary with updated burst-window config later today. I'll open a follow-up ticket to adjust default client guidance and update the rollout playbook.

lucas (Eng SRE): logging action items: (1) add per-account allowlist for quick rollback (2) add automatic rollback when retry storms detected (3) tune canary thresholds to consider retry amplification.

tim (Support): tagging PS and AE to keep customer looped.

alice (Support): closing internal loop here, leaving the support ticket open until we confirm no recurring hits in 24h. thanks all.

jun (Eng Platform): will post postmortem notes in #eng-platform after root cause analysis.

lucas (Eng SRE): noted. good run.
